lesson.title: Managing beverage recommendations and varied dietary needs
lesson.reading: いんりょうていあんとたようなしょくじじょうけんをかんりする

objectives.text: Confirm preferences and the menu before recommending a drink
Explain basic sake and wine terminology
Verify and communicate regional, seasonal and cultural food information

sections.title: Begin recommendations by asking preferences
sections.body: To recommend a drink with food, check the menu and the guest’s preferences together. Getting a guest to buy a more expensive item is not the sole purpose. Ask what type they would like, explain differences and propose options at a suitable moment. Pairing can affect satisfaction and sales, but do not impose an unwanted order. Ask a sommelier or knowledgeable colleague about features you cannot explain. Accept a refusal pleasantly and keep the meal flowing.

sections.title: Explain sake
sections.body: Understand rice, kōji and water as the principal ingredients of seishu sake. Regional brands offer different products, and chilled, room-temperature and warmed sake are different serving states. Do not assume all products are served at the same temperature: check the product and facility’s method. Do not infer sweetness from a local origin alone. Ask preferences and explain verified features and serving states. Knowing basic ingredients does not guarantee suitability for a dietary condition; check the particular product when needed.

sections.title: Organize wine names
sections.body: Examples of red-wine grapes in the manual are Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir and Syrah; white examples include Chardonnay, Riesling and Sauvignon Blanc. Distinguish grape names from regions. Bordeaux and Burgundy are French examples, and California is an American example. Do not promise a pairing from red or white alone: check the actual menu and product. Instead of reciting a memorized explanation, give concise information that answers the guest’s question.

sections.title: Check local sourcing and dietary conditions
sections.body:
Local production for local consumption means using regional agricultural or fishery products locally, and complements explanations of seasonal menus. Check where the served ingredients actually come from before describing them. Halal considerations may involve ingredients, alcohol, preparation and verifiable certification, rather than only avoiding pork. Vegetarian conditions differ by person; vegan approaches also avoid animal products including eggs and dairy. Do not answer from a label alone: match requested conditions, products and the facility’s actual capability.

The 2024 Type 2 source lists checks for halal food: no pork or pork-derived ingredients, no drinking alcohol, and certification checks for animal ingredients other than pork. The third item carries the qualification “excluding eggs and milk.” Match this exception to the particular certification item and ingredient category. It does not mean all processed products or dishes containing eggs or milk are unconditionally halal-suitable. Check actual products, preparation methods, verifiable certification and the guest’s requirements with the responsible staff.

terms.meaning: An ingredient used in sake making and other production
Using locally produced goods in the same region
An approach avoiding animal products, including eggs and dairy

example.situation: A guest asks for a drink with a local fish dish, but the server confuses wine grapes with wine regions.
steps: Ask the guest’s preferences and desired drink type.
Check menu and product information, referring unknown points to a specialist.
Explain verified features while distinguishing region, grape and serving state.

practice.prompt: Prepare two recommendations separating brand, grape, region and serving state. Also explain how you would check eggs and dairy for a vegan request.
expectedPoints: Match dietary suitability to product and facility conditions

questions.prompt: What matters first when recommending drinks?
choices: Offer only the highest-priced item
Keep demanding an order after refusal
Confirm the food and the guest’s preferences
Guarantee flavor from region alone without checking
questions.explanation: Confirm preference and food, then recommend at an appropriate time; do not prioritize sales alone.

questions.prompt: Which statement about sake is correct?
choices: Main ingredients include rice, kōji and water; serving examples are chilled, ambient and warmed
The main ingredient is grapes and it is always chilled
All brands are served at one temperature
Region always determines sweetness
questions.explanation: Understand basic ingredients and serving states, then check the actual product’s method.

questions.prompt: Which correctly distinguishes wine variety and region?
choices: Bordeaux is a white grape and Chardonnay a country
California is a grape and Merlot a country
Burgundy is a grape and Syrah a city
Chardonnay is a white-grape example and Bordeaux a French-region example
questions.explanation: A grape and a region are different information. Check the actual wine rather than relying only on color.

questions.prompt: Which response to a vegan request is appropriate?
choices: Eggs and milk are always fine after removing meat
Check actual ingredients and the guest’s conditions, including eggs and dairy
Serve the usual food without asking
Assume every certification is present
questions.explanation: Vegan approaches avoid animal products. Check products and conditions as well as the label.

questions.prompt: Which grape grouping is given in the material?
choices: Red: Merlot and others; white: Chardonnay, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc and others
Red: the country Bordeaux; white: the country California
Every name means the same region
White is always the grape variety warmed sake
questions.explanation: Separate grape varieties from regions and check the actual product’s features.

questions.prompt: Which wine-region grouping appears in the material?
choices: France: the country Merlot; America: kōji
France: Bordeaux and Burgundy; America: California
Bordeaux and Burgundy are exclusively grape varieties
A region alone determines the guest’s preferences
questions.explanation: Explain regions, varieties and product features as distinct information.

questions.prompt: How should local production for local consumption and seasonal ingredients be explained?
choices: A local dish name guarantees all ingredients are local
Call an ingredient seasonal regardless of season
Check actual origin and seasonality and explain their use in the dish
Determine origin from appearance
questions.explanation: Local production for local consumption concerns using local products locally; seasonality concerns an ingredient’s season. Verify before explaining.

questions.prompt: What should you do when halal accommodation has not been verified?
choices: Claim all certifications once pork and alcohol are absent
Decide every condition from origin alone
Serve the normal meal without asking preferences
Check necessary ingredients, preparation conditions and verifiable certification without giving unverified guarantees
questions.explanation: A label alone does not establish specific conditions or certification.

questions.prompt: Which source statement carries “excluding eggs and milk” in the 2024 Type 2 material?
choices: Eggs and milk never need checking in any dish
Eggs make pork or alcohol acceptable
Vegans eat eggs and milk
The item requiring certification checks for animal ingredients other than pork
questions.explanation: The exception applies to the source’s animal-ingredient certification item. It does not guarantee whole dishes containing eggs or milk, and differs from vegan requirements.

questions.prompt: A guest asks whether a pork-free meat dish is halal-suitable. Which check follows the source conditions?
choices: Answer yes immediately because it is not pork
Check meat ingredients, certification, preparation, facility capability and the guest’s conditions
Skip certification for expensive meat
Extend the egg-and-milk exception to all animal ingredients
questions.explanation: The source discusses certification for non-pork animal ingredients separately from avoiding pork-derived ingredients. Do not read this as unconditional suitability whenever pork is absent.

illustration.caption: Distinguish grape, region and serving state to guide guests toward a suitable drink.
illustration.alt: Sake ingredients and chilled/ambient/warmed states shown separately from wine grapes and regions
